newsitem.title: USA: Conrail again rejects Norfolk Southern bid.
newsitem.headline: Conrail again rejects Norfolk Southern bid.

text.p: Conrail Inc., the northeast railroad that is the target of two rivals, Wednesday reconfirmed its intentions to accept an $8.5 billion takeover bid from CSX Corp. and reject a $10 billion hostile bid by Norfolk Southern Corp.
It was the second time that Conrail rejected an offer from Norfolk Southern in favour of its planned union with CSX, which Conrail has repeatedly said provides more strategic benefits.

CSX last week slightly sweetened its cash-and-stock bid for Conrail. Conrail said then its board had considered the merits of the rival bids and reaffirmed that a merger with CSX was superior, despite a higher cash offer by Norfolk Southern.
The merging of CSX and Conrail would create one of the largest transportation companies in the world, including a rail system with some 29,000 miles (47,000 km) of routes in 22 eastern states.

Philadelphia-based Conrail, which operates on 11,000 miles (17,700 kms) of track mostly in 12 northeastern states, said in a statement that its board was recommending that its shareholders not tender their shares to Norfolk Southern.
Instead, Conrail reaffirmed its desire to link up with CSX and said the two freight carriers have been discussing increasing the value of the pact upon consummation of the transaction.
Conrail said, however, that there could be no assurances that its pact with CSX would be modified.

Under the latest CSX offer, it would pay $4.01 billion cash for 40 percent of Conrail's 91 million outstanding shares. It would also offer 1.85619 of a CSX share, or about $4.49 billion based on Wednesday's trading price of $44.375, for the remaining shares.
That would value Philadelphia-based Conrail's shares at about $93.41 each, less than the $110 in cash that Norfolk Southern is offering.
Conrail's stock, which rose Tuesday on views that CSX might again sweeten its offer, lost 75 cents to $96.50 in morning trading Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange.
CSX lost 12.5 cents to $44.50, while Norfolk Southern gained 12.5 cents to $87.875 on the NYSE.
